title: introduce-synthetic-hotspot-phase-workload-generator-and-adaptive-sample-reporter
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: We need a compact, reproducible workload generator that can produce realistic hotspot traffic and explicit phase transitions to exercise cache churn, scheduler fairness, and adaptive batching in the serving runtime. Existing synthetic runners either use static key distributions or sequence-only mixes; they do not drive controlled phase changes or allow per-phase cardinality tuning. This PR introduces a new runner (hotspot_phase_sim) and an accompanying reporting stage that selects samples for CPU and GPU per-sample flamegraphs and KV-cache hit-rate timelines.

What this PR does: Adds a hotspot-and-phase-aware synthetic workload generator that supports: configurable phases (duration, key-cardinality, read/write mix), hotspot shapers (zipf alpha + dynamic hotspot fraction), per-client jitter and skew, and an event stream that emits phase-boundary markers. It also: 1) integrates the runner into the existing job orchestration/benchmark harness, 2) adds a phase-aware metric exporter that annotates percentile histograms with the active phase id, and 3) implements an adaptive-sample-reporter which picks latency outliers and evenly samples across phases for detailed trace/flamegraph capture.

Why this is different: Unlike the previous sequence-mix and microburst runners, this generator explicitly models long-lived hotspots that drift between keys across phases and combines that with tunable cardinality so teams can reproduce cache thrash vs. stable-hotspot regimes. The adaptive reporter focuses limited instrumentation budget on the most informative samples (phase boundary latencies, sustained p99 regressions) to make profiling runs smaller and faster to analyze.

Backward compatibility: The generator exposes a compat-mode which maps hotspot traffic into the same measurement buckets used by existing microbenchmarks so historical dashboards are comparable. The new exporter adds a single optional metric label "bench_phase" so existing consumers that ignore unknown labels are unaffected.

How to run locally: ./bazel run //benchmark-lab:hotspot_phase_sim -- --config=examples/hotspot_phase/low_cardinality.yaml  (or use --profile to enable adaptive sampling). See examples/hotspot_phase/README.md for common presets.

Performance notes: Initial runs against a 4-GPU dev cluster show the generator can drive sustained 8k reqs/s with 50ms median and 320ms p99 under a heavy-hotspot (alpha=1.2) setting. The adaptive reporter reduced instrumented-samples by ~10x for equivalent understanding of failure modes in our preliminary analyses.

Related work: ENG-2319 (kv-cache regression tests), ENG-2587 (batcher fairness suite), and a draft of the flamegraph sample-picker in PR #31211.

Checklist: - [x] generator implementation - [x] integration tests for phase boundary markers - [x] exporter + metric annotations - [x] example configs and README - [x] unit tests for hotspot shaper RNG - [x] bench harness integration and CI job

Notes for reviewers: The RNG for hotspot key selection uses a seeded combined zipf+uniform sampler for reproducibility; pay attention to seeded tests under benchmark-lab/tests/seeded. The adaptive reporter is intentionally conservative: it never captures more than 0.5% of total requests by default and respects the runtime's instrumentation rate limits.
